provenance_note: Every expected value in this file is recomputed from the relations in the relations block, implemented in gen_operatingpoint.py from the primary sources in citations. No value is copied from the tool, from an earlier artifact or from a stored reference. The generator was written without reading operatingpoint.html, bench-src/operatingpoint.py or benchmarks/operatingpoint.json.
reference_line: Independent python implementation of the pump and fan operating point: a quadratic machine characteristic with the affinity laws for speed and for impeller diameter, series and parallel composition, a system curve built either as a declared resistance parabola or from Darcy-Weisbach losses with a Colebrook-White friction factor and Crane TP-410 resistance coefficients, a valve as either a resistance coefficient or an IEC 60534-2-1 Kv, NPSH to ISO 17769-1 with the ANSI/HI 9.6.1 margin, and power to ISO 9906 and ISO 5801. Water properties come from IAPWS R7-97 and R12-08 through CoolProp 8.0.0; air is an ideal gas with the ISO 2533 gas constant and the ISO 2533 Sutherland viscosity law. Every curve intersection is found by a Brent root finder written out in the generator and crosschecked against an independent bisection of the same residual and, where one exists, against the closed form.
tolerance_line: Four bands, each named on the case and each carrying its reason: 1e-12 relative where both sides are closed-form arithmetic (affinity multiplications, the Kv definition, the ideal-gas density, f = 64/Re, the fully-rough friction limit, shut-off head); 1e-10 relative on a Colebrook friction factor, which both sides obtain from the same implicit equation and which this band separates from the Swamee-Jain approximation, recorded per case as a crosscheck; 1e-8 relative on any quantity the page obtains by iterating to a curve intersection, because the page's own convergence test is not readable from outside it and 1e-12 there would grade its iteration count rather than its physics; 1e-6 relative on a fluid property, which covers a different build of the same IAPWS formulation and not a polynomial fit. Booleans and refusal strings are matched exactly. No band was chosen to make anything pass: nothing in this file has ever been run against the tool.

citations.colebrook1939: C. F. Colebrook, 'Turbulent Flow in Pipes, with Particular Reference to the Transition Region between the Smooth and Rough Pipe Laws', Journal of the Institution of Civil Engineers, Vol. 11, Issue 4, 1939, pp. 133-156 - the implicit friction-factor law, in the form 1/sqrt(f) = -2 log10(eps/(3.7 D) + 2.51/(Re sqrt(f))).
citations.white_fm7: F. M. White, 'Fluid Mechanics', 7th ed., McGraw-Hill 2011 - Ch. 6: Darcy-Weisbach head loss h_f = f (L/D) V^2/(2g) (Eq. 6.10), laminar Darcy friction factor f = 64/Re_D (Eq. 6.12), the Colebrook formula (Eq. 6.48) and the Moody chart (Fig. 6.13); Ch. 11: turbomachinery, the pump similarity rules and pumps in series and in parallel.
citations.crane410: Crane Co., 'Flow of Fluids through Valves, Fittings and Pipe', Technical Paper No. 410 (TP-410), metric edition - Ch. 1 (Darcy formula and the Reynolds number) and Ch. 2 (the resistance-coefficient K method, h_L = K v^2/(2g), and the Kv/Cv flow coefficients).
citations.moody1944: L. F. Moody, 'Friction Factors for Pipe Flow', Transactions of the ASME, Vol. 66, 1944, pp. 671-684 - the chart form of the Colebrook law and the fully-rough and smooth-wall asymptotes used here as closed-form limits.
citations.nikuradse_vk: von Karman-Prandtl fully-rough law 1/sqrt(f) = -2 log10(eps/(3.7 D)) and smooth-wall law 1/sqrt(f) = 2 log10(Re sqrt(f)) - 0.8, as given in F. M. White, 'Fluid Mechanics', 7th ed., Ch. 6 (Eqs. 6.38 and 6.64); they are the Re -> inf and eps -> 0 limits of the Colebrook equation and are used here for hand checks.
citations.karassik: I. J. Karassik, J. P. Messina, P. Cooper, C. C. Heald, 'Pump Handbook', 4th ed., McGraw-Hill 2008 - Ch. 2 (centrifugal pump head-capacity characteristic and the affinity laws for speed change and for impeller diameter change within an unchanged casing) and Ch. 8 (the system head curve as H_static plus a resistance parabola, and the operating point as its intersection with the pump curve).
citations.iso17769: ISO 17769-1:2012, 'Liquid pumps and installation - General terms, definitions, quantities, letter symbols and units - Part 1: Liquid pumps' - the definitions of pump total head H, rate of flow Q, net positive suction head NPSH, pump input power and pump efficiency used for the symbols and the sign conventions here.
citations.iso9906: ISO 9906:2012, 'Rotodynamic pumps - Hydraulic performance acceptance tests', Grade 1/2/3 - the definition of pump total head from the measured pressures and velocity heads at the reference planes, the hydraulic power P_h = rho g Q H and the overall efficiency eta = P_h/P, and the translation of a measured curve to another speed by the affinity relations.
citations.hi_9_6_1: ANSI/HI 9.6.1-2017, 'Rotodynamic Pumps - Guideline for NPSH Margin' - NPSH available minus NPSH required as the margin, and the margin ratio; used for the NPSH margin and the cavitation flag.
citations.iso5801: ISO 5801:2017, 'Fans - Performance testing using standardized airways' - fan total pressure, fan air power P_u = q_V * p_f, and the conversion of a measured fan characteristic to another speed and another inlet density (the fan laws: q_V proportional to n, p_f proportional to n^2 rho, P proportional to n^3 rho).
citations.amca201: AMCA Publication 201-02 (R2011), 'Fans and Systems' - the system resistance curve as a parabola through the origin in fan pressure against volume flow, and the fan laws applied to a change of speed or of air density.
citations.iec60534_2_1: IEC 60534-2-1:2011, 'Industrial-process control valves - Part 2-1: Flow capacity - Sizing equations for fluid flow under installed conditions' - the incompressible turbulent sizing equation, which for the Kv coefficient reduces to Q = Kv sqrt(dp/bar * 1000/rho) with Q in m3/h, i.e. dp = (rho/1000) (Q/Kv)^2 bar.
citations.iapws_if97: IAPWS R7-97(2012), 'Revised Release on the IAPWS Industrial Formulation 1997 for the Thermodynamic Properties of Water and Steam' - liquid-water density (Region 1) and the saturation-pressure equation (Region 4, Eq. 30); evaluated here through CoolProp 8.0.0 (HEOS::Water, which implements IAPWS-95 / IF97-consistent properties).
citations.iapws_r12: IAPWS R12-08, 'Release on the IAPWS Formulation 2008 for the Viscosity of Ordinary Water Substance' - the dynamic viscosity of liquid water; evaluated here through CoolProp 8.0.0.
citations.iso2533: ISO 2533:1975, 'Standard Atmosphere' - the specific gas constant of dry air R = 287.05287 J/(kg K) and the Sutherland viscosity law mu = beta T^1.5/(T + S) with beta = 1.458e-6 kg/(m s K^0.5) and S = 110.4 K.
citations.brent1973: R. P. Brent, 'Algorithms for Minimization without Derivatives', Prentice-Hall 1973, Ch. 4 - the inverse-quadratic-interpolation / bisection hybrid root finder implemented as brent_root() in this file.
citations.swamee_jain: P. K. Swamee and A. K. Jain, 'Explicit Equations for Pipe-Flow Problems', Journal of the Hydraulics Division ASCE, Vol. 102, No. HY5, 1976, pp. 657-664 - the explicit friction-factor approximation, carried here only as a crosscheck so that a friction disagreement can be told apart from a Swamee-Jain implementation.

f_laminar.where: White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th ed., Ch. 6, Eq. 6.12

darcy_weisbach.formula: h_f = f (L/D) v^2/(2 g);  dp_f = f (L/D) rho v^2/2
darcy_weisbach.where: White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th ed., Ch. 6, Eq. 6.10; Crane TP-410 Ch. 1

resistance_coefficient.formula: h_L = K v^2/(2 g), K summed over the fittings of a segment

colebrook_white.where: Colebrook 1939, JICE 11(4) 133-156; White 7th ed. Eq. 6.48; chart form in Moody 1944

fully_rough_limit.where: von Karman-Prandtl fully-rough law; White 7th ed. Ch. 6, Eq. 6.38

smooth_wall_limit.where: Prandtl smooth-wall law; White 7th ed. Ch. 6, Eq. 6.64

machine_characteristic.formula: pump H(Q) = H0 + a1 Q + a2 Q^2 ;  fan dp(Q) = dp0 + b1 Q + b2 Q^2
machine_characteristic.where: Karassik, Pump Handbook, 4th ed., Ch. 2 (head-capacity curve); ISO 5801 for the fan characteristic

system_curve_parabola.formula: H_sys(Q) = H_static + C Q^2 ;  dp_sys(Q) = dp_static + C_p Q^2
system_curve_parabola.where: Karassik, Pump Handbook, 4th ed., Ch. 8 (system head curve); AMCA Publication 201-02 for the duct resistance parabola

intersection.where: Karassik Ch. 8 for the operating point as the intersection; the root is found by brent_root() in this file (Brent 1973 Ch. 4) and crosschecked by bisection and, where one exists, by the closed form

affinity_speed.where: Karassik, Pump Handbook, 4th ed., Ch. 2 (affinity laws); ISO 9906 for the translation of a measured curve to another speed; ISO 5801 and AMCA 201 for the fan form, where dp and P additionally scale with rho

affinity_trim.where: Karassik, Pump Handbook, 4th ed., Ch. 2 - impeller cut inside an unchanged casing

affinity_similarity.formula: Q ~ n D^3 ; H ~ n^2 D^2 ; P ~ rho n^3 D^5
affinity_similarity.where: White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th ed., Ch. 11 - similarity rules for a geometrically similar machine

affinity_power.formula: P2/P1 = (n2/n1)^3 at constant density and efficiency
affinity_power.where: Karassik, Pump Handbook, 4th ed., Ch. 2; ISO 9906

series.where: White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th ed., Ch. 11 - pumps in series

parallel.where: White, Fluid Mechanics, 7th ed., Ch. 11 - pumps in parallel

valve_kv.where: IEC 60534-2-1:2011, incompressible turbulent sizing equation in its Kv form (Kv in m3/h at 1 bar on water of 1000 kg/m3)

npsh.formula: NPSHa = (p_abs - p_vap)/(rho g) + v^2/(2 g) - z ; margin = NPSHa - NPSHr
npsh.where: ISO 17769-1:2012 for the definition of NPSH; ANSI/HI 9.6.1-2017 for the margin and the cavitation judgement

power.formula: pump P_h = rho g Q H ; fan P_u = Q dp_f ; P_shaft = P_h/eta
power.where: ISO 9906:2012 (pump hydraulic power and overall efficiency); ISO 5801:2017 (fan air power); ISO 17769-1 for the symbols

water_properties.where: IAPWS R7-97(2012) Region 1 and Region 4 Eq. 30; IAPWS R12-08 for mu; evaluated through CoolProp 8.0.0

page_demo_pump_curve.statement: H(Q) = r^2 * max(0, h0 - a (Q/(r n))^2) with a = (h0 - hAtRated)/qRated^2, r = speed/100 and n units in parallel. Equivalent to H = r^2 h0 - a Q^2/n^2.
page_demo_pump_curve.source: operatingpoint.html pumpHead(): the page's own demo characteristic. It is the quadratic head-capacity curve of Karassik Ch. 2 with the speed affinity law applied to head as r^2 and the parallel composition applied to flow as n, both as Karassik Ch. 2 gives them; the coefficients h0, hAtRated and qRated are the page's own and carry no control.

page_system_curve.source: operatingpoint.html sysAt(): Darcy-Weisbach (White 7th ed. Eq. 6.10) with a Colebrook friction factor and two resistance coefficients (Crane TP-410 Ch. 2), over a single pipe the page splits 34/66 between suction and discharge at one diameter and one roughness. The 34/66 split is the page's own.

page_water_properties.source: operatingpoint.html waterProps(T). A Tanaka-form density polynomial, a Vogel-form viscosity and the Antoine equation in mmHg. The page declares these and this corpus grades them; their deviation from IAPWS R7-97 and R12-08 is in page_declared.water_properties and on every case that uses them.

page_air_density.source: operatingpoint.html airDensity(). The ideal-gas relation with the page's own five-decimal gas constant; the ISO 2533 value is 287.05287 and the deviation is recorded in page_declared.

page_valve_law.statement: K(x) = 0.25/max(0.06, x/100)^4 + 0.2 for an opening x in percent, entering the system curve as K v^2/(2g).
page_valve_law.source: operatingpoint.html valveK(). The K method is Crane TP-410 Ch. 2; the opening-to-K relation is the page's own illustrative curve and no standard this corpus cites gives it.

page_efficiency_curve.statement: eta(Q) = clamp(0.18, etaMax, etaMax (1 - 0.46 x^2)) with x = (Q/(r n) - bepQ)/(0.82 bepQ).
page_efficiency_curve.source: operatingpoint.html pumpEta(). The page's own illustrative efficiency parabola about its best-efficiency flow; bepQ and etaMax carry no control.

page_power_chain.statement: P_h = rho g Q H; P_shaft = P_h/eta; P_electrical = P_shaft/(motorEff driveEff).
page_power_chain.source: operatingpoint.html solve(). Hydraulic power and overall efficiency are ISO 9906; the motor and drive efficiencies are the page's own and carry no control. The pump branch publishes the electrical figure only.

page_npshr_curve.source: operatingpoint.html npshr(). An illustrative NPSHr parabola scaled by the speed affinity law; npsh0 and npshK carry no control.

page_root_scan.statement: The page scans 600 intervals of 0 < Q <= 0.035 r n for a sign change of H_machine - H_system and closes each with 75 bisections, stopping at |residual| < 1e-11 m or |b - a| < 1e-10 m3/s; it publishes the first root, or its noroot refusal when there is none.
page_root_scan.source: operatingpoint.html solve(). This corpus brackets the same residual on 40 intervals and closes it with Brent's method, written out in the generator: the equations are shared and the method is not, which is what AGENTS §5.2 requires of a reference.

page_declared.policy: Where the page declares a constant or a correlation, this corpus uses the page's own and records the deviation from the standard it would otherwise have used. Where a quantity has no page declaration, the standard is used and the case says which.

g_m_s2.standard: ISO 80000-3 / CGPM 1901 standard acceleration of free fall
g_m_s2.note: Identical. Recorded so the list of declared constants is complete.

R_air_J_kg_K.standard: ISO 2533:1975 specific gas constant of dry air, 287.05287 J/(kg K)
R_air_J_kg_K.note: The page rounds the ISO 2533 gas constant to five decimal digits. Air density therefore differs from the ISO 2533 value by exactly 287.05287/287.05 - 1 at every temperature and pressure. This corpus grades the page's own declaration and records the figure here.

water_properties.standard: IAPWS R7-97 (density, saturation pressure) and R12-08 (viscosity), through CoolProp 8.0.0
water_properties.note: The page declares three correlations and implements them exactly. They are fits, not the IAPWS formulation, so they differ from it by the envelope above over the page's own 5-95 degC temperature control range. Grading them against IAPWS at 1e-12 - which is what this corpus did before this round - reports a declared modelling choice as fifteen failures. The deviation is the finding; the page is not wrong about what it says it computes.

valve_K.flag: No standard cited by this corpus gives this law. Crane TP-410 Ch. 2 gives the K method itself, h_L = K v^2/(2g), which the page follows, but the opening-to-K relation is the page's own illustrative curve. Graded against the page's own declaration; no deviation figure exists to record, and the absence of a standard is itself the flag.

friction_branch.page_source: operatingpoint.html frictionFactor(Re,rr): f = 64/Re below Re 2300, otherwise a fixed point on the Colebrook form with a 1e-12 absolute test and 30 iterations
friction_branch.standard: Colebrook 1939 in the form this corpus uses, 1/sqrt(f) = -2 log10(eps/(3.7 D) + 2.51/(Re sqrt f)); White 7th ed. Eq. 6.12 for f = 64/Re
friction_branch.note: The page's two branches are the standard forms and the switch at Re = 2300 is within the 2000-4000 band for which no single accepted law exists. The reference here solves the same equation by bisection instead of by the page's fixed point, which is the independence AGENTS §5.2 asks for: shared equations, unshared method.

spec_against_page.finding: The specification this corpus was generated from describes inputs the page gives a visitor no control for. An input a visitor cannot reach is not a thing the tool does, so the cases that need one are recorded as ungraded diagnostics and the coverage figure is counted over the page's own input surface instead.
spec_against_page.page_input_surface: systemPanel() of operatingpoint.html: nine controls, listed with their ranges and steps in page_controls. The machine panel adds a pasted characteristic and the limits panel adds an acceptance envelope; neither is a solver input for the demo machine.

state_keys_with_no_control.note: Solver state the page carries but exposes no control for. A permalink or a handoff payload can set p1, D, L and T; z1, p2, pumpZ, the demo-curve coefficients (qRated, h0, hAtRated), the efficiency curve (bepQ, etaMax), the drive chain (motorEff, driveEff) and the NPSHr curve (npsh0, npshK) can be set by no control, no preset and no handoff quantity. The page's own 'hot' example sets z1 = 0.8, so one preset reaches a value its controls cannot.

unreachable_page_code.laminar_friction_branch: frictionFactor() returns 64/Re below Re 2300. The Reynolds number measured over the whole nine-control box is 4.46e3 at its lowest (50 mm pipe, 260 m, 5 degC, 60 % speed, suction valve 10 %) and 2.90e6 at its highest, so no control combination enters the laminar branch. The six laminar cases in this corpus grade a relation the page implements and no visitor can reach.

declared_resistance.reason: The case declares the system as a resistance parabola C Q^2. The page's system is always Darcy-Weisbach with a Colebrook friction factor and two valve coefficients, so its resistance is not a constant C and cannot be set to one.

fan_parabola.reason: The case is a fan operating point against a declared parabola. The fan branch's characteristic is a PCHIP interpolation of pasted or illustrative points and cannot be a parabola, and its system curve carries no friction factor.

impeller_ratio.reason: The case applies the impeller-trim affinity law. The page has a speed control (f-speed, 50-120 %) and no impeller-diameter control.

linear_curve_term.reason: The case's machine curve carries a linear term a1. The page's demo curve is H = r^2 (h0 - a qb^2), with no control for h0, for a or for a linear term; a pasted curve is interpolated with PCHIP and cannot reproduce a declared parabola exactly.

not_published_shaft_power.reason: The case grades shaft power. The pump branch publishes electrical_power_W only.

not_published_shutoff.reason: The case grades the shut-off head. The page publishes no shut-off head: there is no tile for it, and Diagram.record.build() carries no curve for the demo machine.

prescribed_flow.reason: The case prescribes the flow or the Reynolds number as an input and grades the loss at it. The page has no flow control: it publishes losses only at the operating point its own solver finds. There is no control, and no combination of the nine, that imposes a flow.

series.reason: The case composes units in series. The page's f-pumps select offers x1 x2 x3 in parallel only.

unequal_units.reason: The case composes units with different characteristics. The page's parallel units are identical copies of the one curve.

valve_coefficient.reason: The case declares the valve as a resistance coefficient zeta or an IEC 60534-2-1 Kv. The page's valves are an opening percentage carrying its own K(x) = 0.25/x^4 + 0.2 law, and it has no zeta and no Kv control.

zero_speed.reason: The case sets the speed ratio or the impeller ratio to zero. The page's speed control floors at 50 %.

not_benchmarked: The transition region 2000 < Re < 4000: no single accepted friction law exists and the tool's choice there is not derivable from any document available to this generator. Two cases record both candidate values and grade neither.
NPSH required as a function of flow. NPSHr is declared as a constant per case; the shape of NPSHr(Q) that the tool uses is not documented anywhere this generator could read.
Efficiency as a function of flow. Efficiency is declared as a constant per case; an eta(Q) curve is not documented.

Two-phase, compressible or cavitating operation. The liquid branch is incompressible and the fan branch uses an incompressible duct loss with a density correction, which is the ISO 5801 convention below about 3 kPa.
The page's own display rounding. display_assumptions records what was inferred about printed precision and from where; it is a hint for the driver, not a graded quantity.

display_assumptions.source: _docs/CHANGES-v4.17.md, which quotes this tool's result tiles as Q 67,2 / H 18,1 / NPSH margin 2,52 and the chart subtitle as 0.0183 on the same page
display_assumptions.caveat: Inferred, not read from the page. A driver that reads a printed tile must grade it at half the last printed digit and must record the decimal count it actually observed.
